title: RSS’s Century of Service Reflects India’s Tradition of Seva: Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan
subtitle: Vice President Releases Dr. Tamilisai Soundararajan’s Book on RSS’s Century of Service
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 SEP 2026 8:43PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan today released the book “A Century of Service – The RSS in 100 Acts of Seva” authored by former Governor of Telangana and former Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry, Dr. Tamilisai Soundararajan, at Uprashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi.
Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan today released the book “A Century of Service – The RSS in 100 Acts of Seva” authored by former Governor of Telangana and former Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry, Dr. Tamilisai Soundararajan, at Uprashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi.
pic.twitter.com/50z9TnIyID
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
September 15, 2026
Addressing the gathering, the Vice President said the book documents the RSS’s century-long service, its social responsibility and its contribution to nation-building.
Observing that “today’s news is tomorrow’s history,” Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan stressed the importance of documenting good work, which could otherwise fade from public memory. He said the book captures how the spirit of seva has translated into sustained social service.
Describing “Seva is Dharma; it is a duty” as a foundational ideal, the Vice President said RSS service initiatives have reached the poor, marginalised and diverse sections of society, including workers, women and children. He recalled the role of RSS volunteers in providing food, medicines and essential support during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Referring to the theme of “Nation-building through character-building” in the book, the Vice President said patriotism, discipline, social responsibility and national unity are essential to nation-building.
He said the book would serve not only as a record of the RSS’s century-long service but also as a document reflecting India’s tradition of seva, culture and national consciousness for future generations.
The Vice President congratulated Dr. Tamilisai Soundararajan and all those associated with the publication, expressing hope that more such efforts to document history would follow.
Union Minister of State for Information & Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan; Puducherry Home Minister Shri A. Namassivayam; Dr. Tamilisai Soundararajan; were present.

title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addresses 25th Anniversary Celebrations of ICWA as an Institute of National Importance
subtitle:
Vice-President Congratulates EAM Dr. S. Jaishankar and the MEA Team on Successful BRICS Summit

Human Progress and World Peace Possible Only When Nations Recognise Each Other’s Concerns and Work for Mutual Benefit: Vice-President

“India Is Emerging on Global Stage as a Strong Voice for Peace, Progress & Prosperity”: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 SEP 2026 2:34PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President and President, Indian Council of World Affairs (ICWA), Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed the 25th Anniversary celebrations of ICWA as an Institution of National Importance at Sapru House, New Delhi. He said the Silver Jubilee was an occasion for gratitude and reflection and paid tribute to the founders, former leaders, Directors General, scholars, diplomats, researchers and staff who have contributed to the Council’s distinguished legacy.
Vice President of India and President, Indian Council of World Affairs (ICWA), Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the 25th Anniversary celebrations of ICWA as an Institution of National Importance at Sapru House, New Delhi today.
The Vice President emphasised that human…

The Vice-President congratulated External Affairs Minister and Vice-President of ICWA, Dr. S. Jaishankar, Foreign Secretary Shri Vikram Misri and the entire team of the Ministry of External Affairs for the successful hosting of the BRICS Summit. He said that in a world disturbed by conflicts and contradictions, the unanimous adoption of the New Delhi Leaders’ Declaration was a significant achievement.
He emphasised that the first objective of diplomacy is to build good relations among nations. Human progress and world peace must go hand in hand, and this is possible only when countries recognise each other’s concerns and work towards mutual benefit, he said.
Highlighting India’s growing global role under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice-President said India has emerged as a strong voice for peace, progress and prosperity. He highlighted Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, the world is one family, and cited Vaccine Maitri during Covid crisis, India’s disaster-response efforts, LiFE and global initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance and Global Biofuel Alliance as examples of this philosophy in action.
The Vice-President highlighted India’s achievements in UPI and Digital Public Infrastructure, observing that “transparent payment systems lead to transparent governance.” He said India is sharing its technological and institutional capabilities with the Global South through ITEC and educational collaborations, including the first IIT campus outside India in Zanzibar. “India is emerging on the global stage to lead the Global South,” he said, noting the growing trust and confidence of India’s international partners.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said the changing global environment has made ICWA’s role even more important. He outlined four priorities for the Council: strengthening research on India’s Neighbourhood First, Act East, Global South and Indo-Pacific priorities; expanding work on cyber security, space, critical technologies and global supply chains; deepening engagement with universities and young scholars; and becoming a reliable repository of knowledge on world affairs with an authentic Indian perspective.
The Vice-President said ICWA must prepare itself intellectually and institutionally for Viksit Bharat @ 2047 and work towards becoming one of the world’s respected centres for the study of international affairs. He expressed confidence that the Council would make even greater contributions to India and a peaceful world order by its Golden Jubilee.
The Vice-President also visited a photo exhibition showcasing ICWA’s journey and evolution and presented mementos to former Directors General in recognition of their contributions to the Council.

title: INDIAN PARLIAMENTARY DELEGATION PARTICIPATES IN 69TH COMMONWEALTH PARLIAMENTARY CONFERENCE IN CAPE TOWN FROM 12 TO 19 SEPTEMBER 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 SEP 2026 8:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
An Indian Parliamentary Delegation led by Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha is participating in the 69th Commonwealth Parliamentary Conference (CPC) being held in Cape Town, South Africa, from 12 to 19 September 2026.
The Indian Parliamentary Delegation comprises Shri C. Sadanandan Master, MP, Rajya Sabha; Dr. D. Purandeswari, MP, Lok Sabha; Shri Vishnu Datt Sharma, MP, Lok Sabha; Shri Sudheer Gupta, MP, Lok Sabha; Shri Krishna Prasad Tenneti, MP, Lok Sabha; Smt. Rachna Banerjee, MP, Lok Sabha; and Shri P. C. Mody, Secretary General, Rajya Sabha.
The Conference is also being attended by 32 Presiding Officers and 18 Secretaries from State/UT Legislatures of India, who are members of the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA).
Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, arrived in Cape Town today and held bilateral meeting with Hon. Angela Thokozile Didiza, Speaker of the National Assembly, Hon. Poobalan Govender, Deputy Chairperson of the National Council of Provinces of South Africa and Hon. Annelie Lotriet, Deputy Speaker of National Assembly. The meetings provided an opportunity to exchange views on matters of mutual parliamentary interest and to further strengthen the close and longstanding parliamentary relations between India and South Africa.
Further, Dr. D. Purandeswari, MP, Lok Sabha, attended the meeting of the CPA Executive Committee and effectively put forth India’s views and perspectives on various matters concerning the CPA.
During the Conference, six main workshops will inter-alia be held on a range of contemporary issues of relevance to Commonwealth legislatures. Shri Harivansh will address the General Assembly of the 69th CPC on the theme, “New Leadership Opportunities for the Commonwealth: Parliamentary Action to Strengthen Democracy and International Law.”
Members of the Indian Parliamentary Delegation, along with Presiding Officers and other representatives from State/UT Legislatures, will participate in the various workshops, plenary sessions and deliberations of the General Assembly during the Conference.
India’s participation in the 69th CPC reflects its continued commitment to strengthening parliamentary democracy, legislative cooperation and inter-parliamentary engagement within the Commonwealth, while further deepening the strong parliamentary ties between India and South Africa.
The Indian delegation will continue its participation in the Conference in the coming days, including in the General Assembly and various workshops addressing issues of contemporary global and parliamentary relevance.

title: Conventional to Smart Mining: Technology Transformation of Coal India Limited
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 SEP 2026 11:20AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Coal mining remains central to India’s energy security and industrial growth. CIL has driven a strategic shift towards modernising both underground (UG) and open-cast (OC) operations for greater efficiency, safety and sustainability. It has rapidly moved away from the conventional mining technology and methods to more advanced tools and practices. Advanced digital interventions – IoT, AI and data analytics – are reducing hazard exposure, improving recovery rates and enabling predictive maintenance, smart control rooms, automated dispatch and ‘Smart Mines’.
The Present: Technology in Action Today
Exploration
Resources are detected using invasive (core drilling) and non-invasive 2D/3D seismic survey, which reduces boreholes by up to 50% and, with Spectral Enhancement (SPE) assaying, sharply improves determination efficiency. Machine-learning techniques (SVM, Decision Tree, Random Forest, MLP, XGBoost) interpret banded coal seams from Gamma-ray, Density and Resistivity logs. CMPDI applies remote sensing, GIS, LiDAR, drones and bathymetric surveys across pre-, syn- and post-mining stages. CIL has signed an MoU with NRSC to develop an AI-powered satellite-based geo-spatial dashboard for mine monitoring and environmental auditing.
Open-Cast Mines
CIL is progressively deploying higher-capacity HEMM – 42 CuM shovels, 240 te dumpers, draglines and surface miners for blast-free mining – standardised since 2021. Blast-free technology minimises dust, noise and vibration while improving product quality and reducing coal loss. Electric detonators were phased out in 2024-25 in favour of ultra-safe electronic detonators. AI-based safety features – operator fatigue monitoring, proximity warning, 360° cameras and automatic fire detection/suppression – are being incorporated in major HEMM, supported by AI simulators and VR training. Digitalisation through GPS-based truck dispatch/OITDS, payload monitoring (PLMS) and vehicle health monitoring (VHMS) further improves utilisation.
Underground Mines
CIL is committed to raising UG production to around 100 MT using Continuous Miner, Longwall and Highwall technology. Continuous mining is already adopted, with large-scale Longwall now being introduced. Major investments are planned in Paste Fill to unlock high-grade coal otherwise locked in pillars, alongside enhanced ventilation and strata management to strengthen safety.
Major Infrastructure Execution
CIL is strengthening coal evacuation through First Mile Connectivity (FMC) and critical railway infrastructure. Of 92 planned FMC projects integrating CHPs, silos, conveyors and Rapid Loading Systems, 46 are commissioned – creating about 432 MTPA capacity – with the ~₹27,800 crore programme targeting 994 MTY mechanical loading capacity by FY 2029-30. Complementing this, four of seven critical railway projects (~₹23,465 crore) are commissioned, with the rest targeted by FY 2027-28. High-angle/sandwich conveyors are being adopted for in-pit transport in place of HEMM.
Coal Processing & Environment Management
Beneficiation technologies – Heavy Media Cyclone, Hydro Cyclone, Teeter Bed Separator, Reflux Classifier and Jigs – are operational across CIL washeries. On the environment side, CIL’s inventory is at par with global levels, with continued focus on real-time monitoring and efficient, cleaner applications.
IT Initiatives & Digital Transformation
CIL’s digital landscape rests on two pillars. In Operational Technology (OT), CIL has deployed Integrated Command and Control Centres (ICCCs), Vehicle Tracking, RFID systems, weighbridge automation and GPS fleet monitoring, with the DigiCoal pilot covering seven mines. In Enterprise IT, CIL has implemented SAP S/4HANA, e-Office, cloud infrastructure and data analytics – integrating procurement, inventory, finance and HR, enabling paperless file movement and faster, data-driven decisions.
The Future: Roadmap to Intelligent, Green Mining
Next-Generation Mining
The next phase moves towards intelligent, autonomous and low-carbon mining. Remote-operated Line-of-Sight dozers are being piloted in SECL and NCL (approx. ₹2.0 Cr per equipment), with electric mobility and Trolley Assist technology planned for 190T+ diesel-electric dumpers. CIL is working with IIT Madras on safe electrification of fossil-fuel equipment. In UG mines, 5G networks, digital twins and autonomous monitoring rovers are being developed for communication, automation and simulation.
Smart Infrastructure, Processing & Environment
Smart conveyor systems with PLC-based HMI and IoT-enabled monitoring of speed, load and temperature for remote command and control.
Dry beneficiation of coal – Air Table, Dry Jigging, Coal Winnowing and XRT sorting – under active exploration.
Real-time CAAQMS and CEQMS monitoring, AI-based dust prediction, GIS/satellite/drone monitoring, Zero Liquid Discharge systems and large-scale overburden-to-sand utilisation.
Digital & Enterprise Roadmap
CIL envisages 5G, IoT, AI/ML, edge computing and advanced automation to enable real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance and remote operations, progressively creating connected, automated and data-driven mines. The Bhuvan Geospatial Dashboard is being developed with NRSC to monitor coal fires, mine closure, afforestation and R&R. The 17 DigiCoal solutions tested in 7 mines will be replicated across all mega mines, alongside strengthened Information Security Management (ISMS).
Research & Development
CIL’s R&D thrust gained momentum in FY2024-25 with the National Centre for Coal and Energy Research (NaCCER), a hub-and-spoke centre shifting focus from proof-of-concept to prototype development (TRL-4 and above). Three Centres of Excellence – CLEANZ (IIT Hyderabad), CSE (IIT Madras) and IMiN (IIT-ISM Dhanbad) – host 13 high-TRL and 11 low-TRL projects. Key projects include Underground Coal Gasification (Kasta, ECL), 5G in OC and UG mines, indigenous Perovskite Solar Cells (with IIT Bombay) and 500-tonne Self-Advancing Goaf Edge Supports (SAGES) under trial at Churcha UG Mine, SECL.
R&D Roadmap to FY 2030
Investment of ₹1,900 Cr by FY30 for R&D projects and Centres of Excellence.
Pilot-scale plants for gasification, battery recycling and coal-based membranes; new CoEs at IIT Bombay/Roorkee/Kharagpur/Delhi and a dedicated centre in North-East India.
A Pilot Integrated Coal Refinery Complex, permanent NaCCER centre, and emerging projects in hydrokinetic pumped storage, coated spherical purified graphite and dry coal beneficiation.
The Indian mining sector still faces challenges – large capital needs, skilled manpower and adapting global technologies to diverse geologies. CIL’s trajectory is defined by deeper integration of automation, robotics, AI and green mining technologies, backed by capacity building and enabling policy – keeping innovation, research and skill development central to a safe, efficient and sustainable mining ecosystem.

title: CCPA Imposed ₹10 Lakh Penalty on Rapido for Misleading Tipping Prompts and Dark Patterns
subtitle:
CCPA finds “Confirm Shaming” and “Interface Interference” in Rapido’s ride-booking interface

CCPA directs Rapido to discontinue misleading prompts and practices that steer consumers towards paying more

CCPA’s action follows sector-wide examination of advance-tipping and dynamic pricing practices by ride-hailing platforms
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 SEP 2026 5:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The
Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA)
, headed by
Chief Commissioner Smt. Nidhi Khare
and
Commissioner Shri Anupam Mishra
, has imposed a
penalty of ₹10 lakh on Roppen Transportation Services Private Limited
, which operates the ride-hailing platform
Rapido
, for
misleading advertisements, unfair trade practices, unfair contract and dark patterns
in the manner in which riders were prompted to pay more before their rides were confirmed.
The action follows a
sector-wide examination of cab and bike-taxi aggregator platforms operating in India
undertaken by CCPA to examine practices relating to
pre-ride tipping and dynamic pricing
. During its examination of various platforms, CCPA found that the Rapido app displayed prompts such as
“Higher the price, higher the chance of getting a ride”
and
“Captains aren't accepting at ₹60. Try adding +10, +20, +30”
while a rider’s booking was still being processed.
CCPA finds prompts amount to “Confirm Shaming”
CCPA found that Rapido’s algorithm first quoted a fare to the rider and, after the rider booked at that fare, prompted the rider to pay more on the ground that Captains were not accepting the original price. CCPA held that this practice creates a
false impression that a rider’s chances of getting a ride quickly depend on paying an additional amount
, at the precise stage when the rider has already committed to the booking and has limited scope to negotiate.The practice was held to constitute
“Confirm Shaming”
, a dark pattern identified under the
Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023
, as it creates a sense of urgency and fear of losing the ride if the consumer does not agree to pay more.
Colour-coded pricing slider found to be a second dark pattern
CCPA also examined Rapido’s
“Set your price”
slider and found that it was colour-coded to influence the rider’s pricing decision.
Raising the price displayed
“higher chance of getting a ride”
in green.
Lowering the price triggered a
red or orange warning
.
The slider provided
more room to increase the price than to decrease it
.
CCPA held that this amounted to a second dark pattern
“Interface Interference”
as the design of the interface visually steered consumers towards paying a higher amount, independent of the accompanying text.
Advance payment cannot be presented as a genuine “tip”
CCPA noted that the fare displayed to a rider at the time of booking already takes into account factors including
distance, time, traffic, tolls and the amount payable to the captain
.In this context, CCPA found no justification for subsequently suggesting that the rider pay an additional amount for the same ride before the ride had commenced. CCPA observed that a
tip is ordinarily a voluntary payment made after a service has been rendered
and should not be presented as a condition for the service to be provided.
CCPA also referred to the
Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2025
, which require that any tipping feature be made available
only after completion of the ride
, and not at the time of booking or during the ride. Rapido had argued that tipping is voluntary, that its matching algorithm continues to operate irrespective of whether a rider pays an additional amount, and that the prompts merely reflected real-time negotiation similar to an offline conversation between a rider and a driver.
CCPA rejected these submissions, holding that the
timing and design of the prompts placed pressure on the rider at the very moment when the rider was most dependent on the platform
’s further noted that Rapido had
not placed any data on record demonstrating that paying an additional amount actually increases the likelihood of a rider getting a ride
. The claim was therefore held to be
unsubstantiated and misleading
.
Sector-wide scrutiny of ride-hailing platforms
The action against Rapido forms part of CCPA’s wider scrutiny of
advance-tip and dark-pattern practices across ride-hailing and bike-taxi platforms
. CCPA had earlier issued notices to platforms including
Uber, Ola, Rapido and Namma Yatri
, directing them to comply with the
Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023
and submit self-declarations regarding compliance. CCPA’s examination of
Uber and Ola
in this regard is currently ongoing.
CCPA reiterates commitment to consumer protection
In exercise of its statutory mandate under the
Consumer Protection Act, 2019
, CCPA continues to take proactive measures to protect consumers as a class, prevent unfair trade practices and ensure that no false or misleading advertisement is made in respect of goods or services.Consumers having complaints or grievances relating to
misleading advertisements, unfair trade practices or dark patterns
may register their grievances through the
National Consumer Helpline (NCH) at 1915
or write to CCPA at
com-ccpa@gov.in
.
The Final Order is available on the
CCPA website
.

title: GATC Network Expands to Strengthen Legal Metrology Verification Infrastructure Across the Country
subtitle:

51 Government Approved Test Centres already recognised; network set to expand further

Several States notify GATC Rules in alignment with amended central framework
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:

content:
The
Department of Consumer Affairs, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
, is strengthening the country’s Legal Metrology verification infrastructure through the expanding network of
Government Approved Test Centres (GATCs)
. A fresh round of applications for recognition has received strong response from
industry, laboratories and technical institutions
across the country.
Following amendments to the
Legal Metrology (Government Approved Test Centre) Rules, 2013
, the scope of GATCs has been broadened to cover
23 categories of weighing and measuring instruments
across sectors including healthcare, energy, transport, retail, manufacturing, infrastructure and emerging clean-energy sectors.
The Department has continued to invite eligible
industries, laboratories, engineering colleges, polytechnics, ITIs and testing facilities
to seek recognition as GATCs. Applications were once again invited through the Department’s online portal, with the latest application window receiving active response from prospective applicants.
A number of applications have been received from eligible organisations following the latest call and are presently under process by the Department in consultation with the concerned State Legal Metrology Departments.
The applications are being examined for:
Completeness of documentation;
Adequacy of verification infrastructure;
Availability of qualified technical personnel; and
Site inspection prior to grant of recognition.
With
51 GATCs already recognised
and a healthy pipeline of applications under active consideration, the GATC network is set to expand further in the coming months, widening the base of technically competent verification facilities available to industry and consumers.
Key Highlights
Fresh round of applications for
GATC recognition
invited, with strong response from industry, laboratories and technical institutions.
Applications received are under process, with
site inspections and technical verification
being carried out in coordination with State Legal Metrology Departments.
51 GATCs
have already been recognised, with the network set to expand further as more applications are approved.
Several States have
finalised and notified their own GATC Rules
, aligning them with the amended central framework.
Verification scope covers
23 categories of instruments
, including water, gas and energy meters, breath analysers, vehicle speedometers, weighing instruments and fuel dispensers for petrol, diesel, CNG, LPG, LNG and hydrogen.
The expanded network strengthens
Ease of Doing Business while reinforcing consumer protection
, in line with India’s status as an
OIML Certification Authority
.
Several States align GATC Rules with amended central framework
In a significant development reinforcing the
Centre-State partnership
underpinning the GATC framework, several States have finalised and notified their own GATC Rules in line with the amended central framework. This alignment at the State level is expected to further deepen the reach of the verification ecosystem, enable smoother coordination between
State Legal Metrology Departments and recognised GATCs
, and support faster and more localised verification services for businesses and consumers across the country.
GATCs supplement State Legal Metrology infrastructure
The expansion of the GATC network is a significant step in the Department’s ongoing efforts to modernise India’s Legal Metrology ecosystem. By enabling technically competent private institutions to undertake
verification and re-verification of specified weights and measures
, the initiative supplements the capacity of State Legal Metrology Departments.
This allows Legal Metrology Officers to devote greater attention to:
Market surveillance;
Risk-based inspections;
Enforcement against serious violations; and
Consumer grievance redressal.
Verification covers 23 categories of instruments
The expanded GATC framework covers
23 categories of weighing and measuring instruments
, including:
Water, gas and energy meters;
Breath analysers;
Speedometers used to measure the speed of vehicles;
Weighing instruments; and
Fuel dispensers for
petrol, diesel, CNG, LPG, LNG and hydrogen
.
As the network of GATCs continues to grow, supported by fresh applications and the alignment of State-level rules with the central framework, the Department is steadily building a
larger, more accessible and technologically capable verification infrastructure
. The expansion reflects the combined efforts of the Legal Metrology system to advance
Ease of Doing Business
while simultaneously strengthening
consumer protection and confidence in everyday commercial transactions
.
The Department reiterates its commitment to building a
transparent, technology-driven and self-reliant system of measurement verification
that enhances fairness in trade and protects the interests of consumers across the country.

title: ‘VIMARSH’ DRDO-Industry Synergy Meet: Raksha Mantri unveils key policy initiatives to empower MSMEs & start-ups and launches framework to share software source codes with licensee industries
subtitle:
Nine Licensing Agreements for Transfer of Technology handed over to 13 manufacturing partners; MoUs exchanged to expand industry outreach

Need to expand DRDO-Industry collaboration, integrate MSMEs & start-ups as integral parts into defence supply chain to transform India into a global production hub: Shri Rajnath Singh

“Viksit Bharat goal is to build an economically strong, technologically self-reliant, socially inclusive, environmentally sustainable & strategically secure nation”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 SEP 2026 1:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh unveiled key policy initiatives during ‘VIMARSH’, a DRDO-Industry Synergy Meet, in New Delhi on September 15, 2026. The initiatives include a comprehensive framework to lower technical and financial entry barriers for MSMEs & deep-tech start-ups, offering direct funding, incubation support and dedicated access to DRDO testing facilities. A standardised, secure framework for sharing DRDO-developed software source codes with licensee industries was also launched to accelerate software-defined defence capabilities and obsolescence management.
Nine (09) Licensing Agreements for Transfer of Technology (LAToTS) were handed over to 13 manufacturing partners in the presence of Raksha Mantri to enable commercial production of state-of-the-art systems.
List of LAToTs handed over to Industry
Strategic MoUs were also formally exchanged with the Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers (SIDM) and Laghu Udyog Bharati (LUB) to expand industry outreach and foster grass-roots participation. DRDO also signed a contract with Quality Council of India for System for Advance Manufacturing Assessment and Rating (SAMAR) version 2.0 to benchmark the manufacturing maturity of domestic defence enterprises.
In his address, Raksha Mantri asserted that the DRDO-Industry collaboration should no longer be limited to production alone, but expanded across the entire value chain encompassing research, design, testing, certification, and manufacturing to transform India into a global hub for defence manufacturing. “DRDO possesses knowledge and technology, the industry has scale and manufacturing capability, start-ups bring innovation and agility, and the youth hold the dream of a New India. When these four forces converge and move forward together, no goal is impossible,” he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh underlined that the goal of Viksit Bharat is not merely to build an economically strong nation, but to also make it technologically self-reliant, socially inclusive, environmentally sustainable, and strategically secure. “By 2047, we must achieve Aatmanirbharta in critical technologies, a significant increase in indigenous content, multi-fold growth in defence exports, and a robust presence for India in global supply chains,” he said.
Raksha Mantri enumerated the unprecedented reforms brought about in the defence sector over the past few years under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, including the notification of Positive Indigenisation Lists, ‘Make in India’ initiative, iDEX, ADITI, and the decision to allocate 25% of the defence R&D budget to the private sector to reduce import dependence and move towards self-reliance. He added that grants are being provided to start-ups through the Technology Development Fund, and numerous technologies have already reached the production stage. He highlighted that iDEX has also created a new ecosystem for defence innovation, where start-ups are developing solutions based on actual operational requirements.
Describing start-ups and MSMEs as the new flag-bearers of innovation in India, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that these industries play a pivotal role in achieving the goal of Aatmanirbhar Bharat as they develop components, sub-systems etc. for major defence systems alongside state-of-the-art technologies. He underscored the need to integrate MSMEs and start-ups as integral parts into the defence supply chain alongside large industries, expressing confidence that the new initiatives would create fresh opportunities for industry.
Raksha Mantri highlighted that the new policy initiatives focus on promoting industry-led R&D; providing funding and mentorship to start-ups and MSMEs; fostering academia-industry collaboration; and encouraging investment in futuristic technologies such as AI, quantum computing, hypersonics, and directed energy.
Shri Rajnath Singh stated that as India is rapidly transitioning from a defence importer to an exporter, there are a number of sectors such as drone technology, AI and cyber security where the MSMEs and start-ups can accelerate innovation, and elevate India’s technological and strategic strengths to newer heights. “MSMEs are the backbone of the Indian economy and a critical strength of the defence ecosystem. They need to consistently focus on quality, delivery, innovation, and global standards, while expanding partnerships with large companies,” he said.
Raksha Mantri emphasised that a nation that possesses its own technology holds the power to shape its own future, adding that self-reliance must become an integral part of the country’s character and attitude. “Companies that invest in new and emerging technologies today will become the leaders of tomorrow as in future warfare, the country that leads in technology will secure the strategic advantage,” he added.
Speaking on the occasion, Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D and Chairman, DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh said VIMARSH 2026, centered on the theme ‘Varta se Vikas’, has been strategically designed to align cutting-edge commercial innovation with national defence readiness and systematically integrate private sector capabilities into the core of the defence ecosystem. This forum serves as a key vehicle for transforming the national security framework from a mere transactional buyer-seller relationship into a collaborative, co-created technology ecosystem, he said.
Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh also highlighted the transformation witnessed by the defence sector in the recent years due to the Government’s self-reliance efforts. “The expansion of technology transfer has not only facilitated the establishment of parallel production lines to meet the Defence Forces’ requirements, thereby directly benefiting MSMEs, but has also helped alleviate the constraints that previously hindered a limited manufacturing base. Till date, over 2,300 Technology Transfers (ToTs) have been handed over to more than 1,100 industries. Currently, we have made technologies related to approximately 50 missiles, developed by DRDO, available to the industry to foster increased participation,” he added.
A book titled ‘Defence Systems for Resilient Bharat – Advancing Aatmanirbharta in Defence’, a special compilation documenting significant defence systems developed by DRDO’s technology clusters between 2014 to 2026 was also released during the event, along with the guidelines for Human Resource Outsourcing Service Contracts in DRDO. The guidelines provide a comprehensive framework for formulation of service specifications for the procurement, selection of suitable service providers, contract administration, performance monitoring and compliance with contractual as well as statutory obligations for Human Resource Outsourcing across DRDO labs.
Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay and Distinguished Scientist & Director General (Production Coordination & Services Interaction), DRDO Dr (Smt) Chandrika Kaushik were present on the occasion.
During the Technical Sessions, Directors General of DRDO Technological Clusters outlined technical roadmaps across Aeronautical Systems, Missiles, Armaments, Microelectronics, and Naval Systems. DRDO HQ introduced initiatives aimed at simplifying procedural compliance, fast-tracking facility access, and compressing licensing timelines.
In the High-Level Panel Discussion, senior representatives from DRDO, Department of Defence Production (DDP), and the Defence Forces deliberated on mechanisms for accelerating technology absorption, optimising Development-cum-Production Partner models, and ensuring rapid induction of indigenous technologies into active service.
The flagship event was attended by over 250 defence industry leaders, industry chamber representatives, senior civil and military officials and senior DRDO scientists. Secretary, DPIIT also participated in the meet. Designed to strengthen the national defence-industrial framework, VIMARSH 2026 provided a structured platform to align DRDO’s technological research and emerging deep-tech startups with the established manufacturing ecosystem, creating an agile, transparent, and collaborative environment for private sector participation.

subtitle:
WCEF2026 must embody spirit of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam by developing Practical Circular Solutions for the World: CM (Gujarat), Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel

Repair before Replace, Reuse before Discard, Recover before Waste - India’s Circularity Ethos rooted in Tradition: Shri Bhupender Yadav

Circularity inherently Collaborative - Knowledge, Technology, Finance and Responsibility need to move across Borders and Sectors: Union Environment Minister
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:

                15 SEP 2026 12:20PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav, along with Chief Minister (Gujarat), Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel, inaugurated the World Circular Economy Forum 2026 at Gandhinagar today. The forum is being organised under the theme
'Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity',
from 15th - 18th September
.
Other dignitaries gracing the inaugural session included Minister for Forest, Environment and Climate Change (Gujarat), Shri Arjunbhai Modhwadia; Minister of State for Forests and Environment, Climate Change (Gujarat), Shri Pravinbhai Mali; Ambassador of Finland to India, Ambassador of Finland to India, H.E. Mr. Mikko Kivikoski; Dy. Directoe General (Circular Economy), Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate (Netherlands), Ms. Marieke Spijkerboer; President SITRA, Mr. Atte Jääskeläinen, along with senior officials from the Government of India and Government of Gujarat.
In his special address, Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel said the first-ever hosting of WCEF in South Asia reflects India’s growing global leadership under the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He said Mission LiFE is emerging as a foundation for the global circular economy and expressed confidence that the Forum would showcase practical circular economy practices for the world.
The Chief Minister reflected on Gujarat’s journey towards environmental conservation, while maintaining a balance between development and the environment. Highlighting traditional circular practices, he cited the example of offerings at the Somnath Temple being recycled into reusable resources and generating livelihoods for local communities. He emphasised that the culture of reuse and the concept of converting waste into wealth have long been part of Indian traditions, and called for WCEF to embody the spirit of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam by developing practical circular solutions for the world.
In his keynote address on the occasion, Shri Bhupender Yadav said that for India, the circular economy is “not a new destination; it is a new way of looking at an old wisdom”. He said the principles of reuse, repair and respect for resources have been deeply embedded in India’s social and cultural fabric. “What we now describe in policy language as circularity was once simply common sense in everyday Indian life - repair before replace, reuse before discard, and recover before waste”, he stated. The Minister said the choice is not between growth and the environment, but an opportunity to make growth itself more resource-efficient, resilient and sustainable. “The true measure of a circular economy will not be how much waste we recycle, but how little value we allow to be wasted,” he said, expressing confidence that WCEF 2026 would forge partnerships and solutions for a circular future.
Shri Yadav highlighted that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India has shifted towards a circular economy through regulatory reforms and digital compliance systems, including strengthened sector-specific waste management rules and the introduction of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR). He said the objective is to ensure that “waste should no longer be seen as the end of a product’s journey, but as the beginning of another resource cycle.” As of August 2026, more than 83,000 producers and 4,802 recyclers were registered under various EPR frameworks, with nearly 482.24 lakh metric tonnes of waste processed across regulated waste streams, he informed.
The Minister stressed that regulation alone cannot create a circular economy and that circularity must also begin with how people consume. Referring to Lifestyle for Environment (LiFE), he said a circular economy cannot be built only at the recycling plant, whereas it must begin in the marketplace, continue in homes and ultimately become a habit in daily life. Calling circularity inherently collaborative, the Minister said no country, company or community can close the loop alone, and emphasised the need for knowledge, technology, finance and responsibility to move across borders and sectors. He highlighted India’s international cooperation on the circular economy, including the Resource Efficiency and Circular Economy Industry Coalition (RECEIC) launched during India’s G20 Presidency. The Minister also stated how India's BRICS Chairship has placed the circular economy alongside sustainable lifestyles, ecosystem restoration and adaptation as interconnected priorities.
Addressing the occasion, Shri Arjunbhai Modhvadia recalled Mahatma Gandhi’s message that the Earth has enough to fulfil everyone’s needs, but not everyone’s greed. He said Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had laid the foundation for a circular economy in Gujarat, which is now being advanced under the leadership of Chief Minister Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel, positioning the State as a global hub for circular transition. He called for turning waste into resources and resources into value to build a sustainable and resilient future.
H.E. Mr. Mikko Kivikoski said circularity is not a separate environmental agenda but a fundamental way of thinking about growth and has become an integral part of Finland’s national policy. He highlighted Finland’s ambition to keep resource consumption below 2015 levels by 2035 and noted that over 100 Finnish companies operating in India are working with sustainable technologies and circular principles. He emphasised the need to move circularity upstream by rethinking what is produced and how value can be retained for as long as possible, noting that “the best waste is that which is never created”. He mentioned the elevation of the India-Finland relationship to a strategic partnership, focusing on digitalisation and sustainability.
Ms. Marieke Spijkerboer underlined that the circular transition is an integral part of Dutch industrial policy, with the country aspiring to become fully circular by 2050. She highlighted progress in reducing material consumption, efforts to strengthen the circular economy law and EPR systems, and stressed that international cooperation is imperative to build circular value chains. Noting the participation of over 20 Dutch companies and organisations at WCEF 2026, she lauded India’s energy and ambition in advancing circularity across large companies as well as start-ups.
The dignitaries inaugurated and reviewed the WCEF2026 exhibition at the venue featuring 135 national and international exhibitors, showcasing practical circular solutions. The Forum is witnessing participation of over 3600 cross-sectoral stakeholders from 62 countries, including business leaders, entrepreneurs, innovators, researchers, policymakers, academicians, changemakers and others.  The Dignitaries also released two publications during the Inaugural Session. They are ‘Best Practices for Reuse of Treated Sewage’ and ‘Driving Sustainability - A Guide to India's Circular Economy and EPR Initiatives’.

title: UPI Continues to Remain Free for Peer to Peer Transactions and 96% of Merchant Transactions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 SEP 2026 6:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The new UPI framework introduced has no impact on any person to person transactions. UPI will continue to remain completely free for all person-to-person transactions, irrespective of the amount transferred.
Payments to merchants up to ₹2,000, along with transactions covered under the zero-MDR framework for small merchants, will also remain free. Consequently, approximately 96% of all P2M transactions will remain unaffected. MDR will apply only to specified merchant transactions above ₹2,000.
It is clarified that MDR is neither a tax nor a charge collected by the Government or NPCI. It is distributed among payment ecosystem participants, including banks and payment application providers, to support the operation and continued expansion of the UPI ecosystem.
Introduced under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, following detailed deliberations by the UPI Steering Committee, the framework seeks to ensure the long-term sustainability of UPI while protecting individuals and small merchants from additional charges.
What Will Remain Free
All Person-to-Person Transactions
: All person-to-person (P2P) UPI transactions will remain completely free, irrespective of the amount transferred. No transaction fee, platform fee or other charge may be imposed on individuals for sending or receiving money through UPI. Therefore, UPI transactions accounting for 70% of the total transaction value will remain completely outside the MDR framework.
Merchant Payments Up to
₹
2,000:
All person-to-merchant (P2M) transactions up to ₹2,000 will remain free of MDR. Customers will not be required to pay any charge when making such payments through UPI.
Payments Received by Small Merchants:
Small merchants including street vendors receiving up to ₹1 lakh per month through UPI QR codes under the Person-to-Person-Merchant (P2PM) category will continue to enjoy zero MDR on all transactions.
This provision will protect street vendors, neighbourhood shops and other small businesses from additional payment costs.
What Will Attract MDR
Merchant Transactions Above
₹
2,000:
A nominal MDR of 0.4% will apply only to P2M transactions above ₹2,000.
The MDR will be shared among payment ecosystem participants, including banks, payment service providers and UPI application providers.
For transactions of ₹75,000 and above, the MDR will be capped at ₹300 per transaction.
Transactions in Essential Sectors:
Transactions above ₹2,000 in essential and thin-margin sectors, including railways, telecommunications, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs, will attract a flat MDR of ₹5 per transaction.
The flat charge will provide cost certainty for critical public services and businesses operating on narrow margins.
Capital Market Transactions:
Payments relating to mutual funds, securities, stockbrokers and dealers will attract an MDR of
0.02%, capped at
₹
300 per transaction
.
The lower rate is intended to support continued retail participation in formal financial markets.
Customers Will Not Pay MDR
MDR is a charge within the merchant payment ecosystem. It is not a charge on customers making UPI payments.
Banks have been advised to ensure that merchants do not pass MDR charges on to customers. UPI application providers are expressly prohibited from imposing platform fees or hidden charges.
Individuals will continue to have unlimited free usage, with no monthly quotas, volume restrictions or tiered caps on free UPI transactions.
Daily transaction limits prescribed by banks and NPCI, generally ranging from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh depending on the transaction category, are security and risk-management safeguards.
They are not charging thresholds.
Most Merchant Transactions Will Remain Unaffected
Data analysis indicates that MDR will apply to only about
4% of merchant transactions
.
This means that
approximately 96% of merchant transactions will remain unaffected
, as they are either below the ₹2,000 threshold or covered by the zero-MDR framework for small merchants.
The framework therefore protects individuals, micro-enterprises and small businesses while introducing a limited charge on larger merchant transactions.
Support for Small Merchants
A dedicated fund will be established to promote UPI adoption among small merchants. An amount equivalent to
5% of total MDR collections
will be contributed to this fund.
The fund will support wider UPI acceptance, sustained usage and the inclusion of small businesses in India’s digital payments ecosystem.
Ensuring the Continued Growth of UPI
The framework has been introduced under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, following detailed deliberations by the UPI Steering Committee on the applicable rates, operational arrangements and consumer safeguards.
The framework seeks to strengthen the long-term sustainability of UPI while keeping payments free for individuals and protecting small merchants.
Revenue generated from larger merchant transactions will support banks, payment service providers and UPI application providers in expanding and improving payment infrastructure, including in rural and semi-urban areas.
The framework is also consistent with the recommendation of the Standing Committee on Finance in its 32nd Report, which emphasised the importance of a viable revenue.

date:

                15 SEP 2026 5:26PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In the presence of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah and Union Jal Shakti Minister Shri C. R. Patil, the Chief Ministers of Uttar Pradesh Shri Yogi Adityanath, Uttarakhand Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami, Himachal Pradesh Shri Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, Rajasthan Shri Bhajan Lal Sharma, Delhi Smt. Rekha Gupta, and Haryana Shri Nayab Singh Saini today signed the Kishau Multipurpose Project agreement. On this occasion, the Union Home Secretary, the Secretary of the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, and the Chief Secretaries of the concerned states were also present.
Addressing the meeting, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that today we have witnessed a historic agreement. He expressed confidence that once the project is completed, this event will become an important chapter in history. He said that the agreement reached today will benefit Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan and Delhi in one way or another. Shri Shah said that the most important aspect is that all six states have given their consent and signed the agreement. Union Home Minister congratulated the Chief Ministers of all six states and Union Minister for Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Patil for playing an important role in bringing the project to this stage. He said that the Government of India and the Chief Ministers of these six states of the Yamuna basin are committed to completing the project at the earliest.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that since Shri Narendra Modi became Prime Minister, this is the tenth water dispute that is now set to be resolved. He said that under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, an initiative has been undertaken to resolve serious disputes that had continued for the past fifty years. He said that first, in August 2018, the dispute over the Lakhwar Multipurpose Project was resolved. In the same month, the dispute over the Shahpur Kandi Dam Project was settled. In 2019, the dispute over the Renukaji Multipurpose Dam Project in the Upper Yamuna Basin was resolved. In 2021, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh reached an agreement on the Ken-Betwa Link Project, benefiting the water-stressed region of Bundelkhand. The revised Parbati-Kalisindh-Chambal River Link project moved forward in 2024. The scheme for transferring water from Hathinikund to the Yamuna through an underground pipeline was approved in February 2024. The dispute over the rehabilitation of families displaced by the Narmada Project was resolved in July 2026. The dispute over water sharing between Bihar and Jharkhand in the Son Basin was settled in August 2026 and today, finally, an agreement has been reached on the Kishau Multipurpose Project.
Shri Amit Shah said that the period from 2018 to 2026, under the leadership of Modi Ji, will be remembered as a period in which almost all water disputes, from Kashmir to Uttar Pradesh, were resolved. He said that the foundation for these resolutions was laid in meetings of the Zonal Councils and the Ministry of Jal Shakti efficiently took these agreements forward. He said that after becoming Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C. R. Patil took upon himself the responsibility of resolving long-pending disputes. He took initiatives at every level and, wherever assistance was required whether it was activating the Inter-State Council or involving the Ministry of Home Affairs, ensured that the task was brought to its conclusion.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that with regard to the Kishau Multipurpose Project, an agreement was reached on 12 May 1994 that separate agreements would be entered into for each storage project coming up in the basin. Without that arrangement, this would not have been possible. Subsequently, after the disputes concerning the Lakhwar and Renukaji projects were resolved in 2019, work on Kishau moved forward. Formal agreement on the project was reached on 16 June this year. The Ministry of Jal Shakti took the matter forward and after securing the consent of all the states, while considering the technical and economic aspects and safeguarding the interests of all the states, brought the matter to a resolution.
Union Home Minister said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India has declared the Kishau Multipurpose Project a National Project. The Government of India will bear approximately 90 per cent of its financial burden, while the remaining 10 per cent will be borne by the participating states in accordance with the 1994 agreement. He said that the Government of Uttarakhand had certain difficulties. On behalf of the Government of India, we have assured them that efforts will be made to accommodate their demands under the schemes of the Government of India, and going forward, we will also assist Uttarakhand in bearing the financial burden that may fall upon the state.
Shri Amit Shah said that a 232.6-metre-high concrete gravity dam will be constructed on the Tons River, which flows along the border of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh, with a water storage capacity of 1,562 million cubic metres. It will irrigate 97,000 hectares of land and generate 1,476 million units of clean hydropower. He said that Delhi will be the biggest beneficiary of the project.
Union Home Minister said that when the waters of the Yamuna were allocated, there was a serious lapse on the part of policymakers. The environmental flow of the Yamuna was not calculated at all, and all the available water was distributed among the states. No water was left for the river itself. He said that 25 per cent of the water will become available through the Kishau Multipurpose Project Agreement, which will prove extremely beneficial for both Delhi and the Yamuna. It will also contribute to environmental conservation.
Shri Amit Shah said that ever since Smt. Rekha Gupta became the Chief Minister of Delhi, continuous work has been underway under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership to clean the Yamuna. He expressed confidence that we will be able to achieve the goal of a clean Yamuna by 2029. When the Yamuna becomes clean, the Ganga also becomes clean, because ultimately the Yamuna merges with the Ganga at Prayagraj. He said that until the dream of cleaning the Yamuna is fulfilled, the dream of a clean Ganga will also remain incomplete.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that the Chief Minister of Delhi and all concerned stakeholders are moving forward with full cooperation and dedication towards making the Yamuna clean. He said that today’s success is an excellent example of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s guiding mantra of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas and Sabka Prayas” and the core mantra of Team India. It also reflects the vision of India in which everyone moves forward together. He expressed confidence that just as all the parties worked with a common purpose and in the same direction to reach this agreement, all the states will similarly work in one direction to complete the project. This will enable us to clean the Yamuna at the earliest and provide crores of people with water for drinking, agriculture, development and industrial use.

title: NDSA Reviews Dam Safety Preparedness and Implementation of Dam Safety Act in Jharkhand
date:

content:
A team of the National Dam Safety Authority (NDSA), led by Shri Saurabh Agrawal, Member (Administration & Finance), NDSA, comprising Shri Manoj Kumar, Senior Joint Commissioner, Department of Water Resources, RD&GR, Ministry of Jal Shakti and Shri Amitabh Meena, Director (Technical), NDSA, held a meeting with the Secretary, Water Resources Department, Government of Jharkhand, on September 8, 2026, to review the implementation of the Dam Safety Act, 2021 and the status of dam safety activities in the State.
The meeting was attended by the Head of the State Dam Safety Organisation (SDSO) and representatives of dam owners from the Water Resources Department, Energy Department and Drinking Water & Sanitation Department (DW&SD) of Jharkhand.
The status of Comprehensive Dam Safety Evaluation (CDSE) of specified dams in Jharkhand was reviewed. NDSA emphasised the need for expeditious constitution of the Independent Panel of Experts (IPoE), timely completion of dam visits and submission of CDSE reports to the Authority. The State was also requested to prepare and furnish a dam-wise action plan for completion of CDSE within the prescribed timeline.
The meeting also reviewed the status of Emergency Action Plans (EAPs) and Operation & Maintenance (O&M) Manuals. Instructions were issued for their timely preparation and subsequent uploading on the DHARMA Portal. The inspection status of Category-II dams was also reviewed and a time bound action plan for rehabilitation of such dams was sought.
NDSA emphasised strengthening of the State's institutional framework for dam safety, including reconstitution of the SDSO as a dedicated organisation rather than a committee-based arrangement. The need for operationalisation of a separate budget head for dam safety and appropriate allocation and utilisation of funds was also emphasised. Capacity-building programmes for dam owners and SDSO personnel were highlighted as an important requirement for strengthening dam safety preparedness in the State.
The importance of timely laying of the SDSO Report before the State Legislature, as required under the Dam Safety Act, 2021, was also emphasised. Representatives of the Energy Department and DW&SD were advised to ensure compliance with the provisions of the Dam Safety Act, 2021 applicable to dam owners under their respective jurisdictions.
The dam owner of Nalkari Dam (Patratu), under the Energy Department, was specifically directed to constitute a Dam Safety Unit (DSU) and undertake pre-monsoon and post-monsoon inspections in accordance with the applicable dam safety regulations.
The Secretary, Water Resources Department, assured the Authority that necessary action would be taken for time bound implementation of the Dam Safety Act, 2021. He directed Head SDSO Jharkhand to prepare a dam wise action plan covering CDSE, EAPs and rehabilitation of Category-II dams and furnish the same to NDSA.
As part of the field level review, the NDSA team visited Nalkari Dam on September 8, 2026 and Latratu Dam, a Category-II dam under the Water Resources Department, on September 9, 2026. The team reviewed the safety aspects and preparedness at the dams. Necessary instructions were issued to the concerned dam in-charges for rectification of deficiencies observed during the visits.
The review reflects NDSA's continued efforts towards strengthening dam safety governance, ensuring compliance with the Dam Safety Act, 2021 and promoting timely preventive and rehabilitative measures for ensuring the safety of dams and downstream communities in the country.

title: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Organises 12th District Collectors’ Peyjal Samvad
subtitle: Six Districts Showcase Innovative Practices on Source Sustainability, Behaviour Change through IEC activities, Grievance Redressal Mechanism and Convergence
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 SEP 2026 5:36PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, organised the
12th edition of the District Collectors’ Peyjal Samvad
today through video conferencing, bringing together senior officials, District Collectors/ District Magistrates/ Deputy Commissioners, to deliberate on accelerating the implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 and sharing of best practices.
The Samvad was chaired by
Shri Ashok K.K. Meena
,
Secretary, DDWS
. Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM) and Senior Officers from SWSM and DDWS were also present during the Samvad.
Addressing the occasion,
Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS
, emphasized the importance of regular monthly District Water and Sanitation Mission (DWSM) meetings to review scheme progress, service delivery, water quality, and source sustainability under JJM 2.0. He stressed that completed schemes should be handed over to Gram Panchayats through the Jal Arpan programme after the prescribed trial run and proper documentation, thereby promoting community ownership and sustainable operation and maintenance. He urged districts to actively involve MPs, MLAs, and other public representatives through Jal Arpan ceremonies, DISHA meetings, and DWSM reviews to enhance transparency and public confidence in rural water supply systems. He also highlighted the need for timely utilization of JJM 2.0 funds, accurate reporting of physical and financial progress, and preparation of District and State Improvement Plans to address service gaps. Further, he encouraged the use of the Decision Support System (DSS) for planning source sustainability measures such as rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge, while underscoring that regular monitoring of scheme functionality, water quality, and sustainability interventions is essential to ensure reliable and sustainable drinking water services for all rural households.
The progress and best practices of six selected districts,
Shahdol (Madhya Pradesh), Samba (Jammu & Kashmir), Hooghly (West Bengal), Dhamtari (Chhattisgarh), Fatehgarh Sahib (Punjab) and North & Middle Andaman (Andaman & Nicobar Islands)
were also presented by the respective District Collectors/District Magistrates/District Commissioners to facilitate cross-learning and support other districts in strengthening implementation under JJM 2.0.
Innovative Best Practices shared by
six districts
through presentations by the respective District Collector/ District Magistrate/ Deputy Commissioner:
Shahdol, Madhya Pradesh- Sh. Parth Jaiswal, District
Collector
informed that civil and electrical works for the water supply schemes have largely been completed, and the remaining works are expected to be commissioned by November 2026. Emphasis was laid on conducting weekly reviews to ensure timely completion of all Single Village Schemes (SVSs) and Multi Village Schemes (MVSs). Out of 544 completed SVSs, 405 have already been handed over, while 35 more are planned for handover on 2 October 2026 through the Jal Arpan programme. The district has set a target to achieve full completion and functionality of all rural water supply schemes by December 2026 and to declare the district fully functional by 26 January 2027. The district also showcased best practices, including a digital platform for overhead tank cleaning and maintenance, an online mechanism for collection of water and sanitation charges through UPI and net banking, and systems to strengthen Gram Panchayat-led operation and maintenance. These initiatives are helping improve transparency, service delivery, revenue collection, and long-term sustainability of rural drinking water infrastructure.
Samba, Jammu & Kashmir- Smt Ayushi Sudan, Deputy Commissioner
presented Samba as a model district under Jal Jeevan Mission, despite facing significant water management challenges due to diverse geographical conditions and dependence on groundwater sources. Through JJM, the district increased Functional Household Tap Connection (FHTC) coverage with prescribed service levels from about 23% to nearly 70%, adding around 35,000 new tap connections. The district implemented 130 water supply schemes, supported by filtration plants, tube wells, dug wells, pumping stations, and storage infrastructure. Key challenges included difficult hilly terrain, declining groundwater levels, source sustainability concerns, power supply constraints, land-related issues, and the high operation and maintenance requirements of water supply systems. To address these challenges, the district adopted location-specific solutions based on local hydrogeological conditions. Several successful interventions were highlighted, including the revival of a 60-year-old dug well at the revered Uttar Behni Temple, which now provides drinking water to hundreds of households, and the development of customized schemes for remote hilly villages through a combination of filtration plants and tube wells to ensure universal coverage.
Hooghly, West Bengal- Sh. Khursheed Ali Qadri, District Magistrate
showcased the district’s substantial progress in creating drinking water infrastructure, the district shifted its focus towards community participation, service assessment, and grievance redressal to ensure sustainable service delivery under Jal Jeevan Mission. Under the Jal Seva Abhiyan, village-level service assessments were conducted by Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSCs), followed by validation exercises. The findings and suggested improvements were incorporated into the District Improvement Plan and submitted to the State Government. A strong emphasis was also placed on community awareness through Self-Help Groups (SHGs), with meetings, workshops, and campaigns involving nearly seven lakh women. These initiatives focused on water conservation, efficient water use, source sustainability, and reducing water wastage. To strengthen accountability, the district established a robust grievance redressal mechanism, receiving complaints through multiple channels, including helplines, emails, public representatives, and government platforms. Dedicated public hearing days are organized every week to address drinking water-related grievances promptly. Strict action has also been taken against illegal water connections and unauthorized usage to prevent water losses and ensure equitable distribution. Regular District Water and Sanitation Committee (DWSC) and DISHA meetings are being conducted with active participation of public representatives to review JJM implementation, address concerns, and undertake corrective measures. These efforts have significantly improved community engagement, transparency, service delivery, and public confidence in rural drinking water systems.
​​​​​​​
Dhamtari, Chhattisgarh- Sh. Abhinash Mishra, District Collector
showcased that the district reported significant progress in the implementation of MVSs, with the majority of schemes already completed and the remaining works expected to be completed after obtaining necessary clearances, particularly in forest and tiger reserve areas. To ensure effective operation and maintenance (O&M), regular DWSM meetings are being conducted twice a month, focusing on scheme sustainability, convergence activities, payment issues, and service delivery improvements. The district has strengthened community ownership by ensuring active participation of VWSCs, with user charges being collected online based on population served. Gram Panchayats have been entrusted with the day-to-day O&M of water supply assets. Special emphasis has been placed on awareness generation through SHGs and community mobilization, with women playing a leading role in water governance. More than two-thirds of the Sarpanches and community representatives involved in these initiatives are women. A notable success story highlighted was a solar-powered Single Village Scheme in a remote tribal habitation, which has significantly improved access to drinking water in difficult terrain. The initiative received wide public appreciation and demonstrated how community participation, renewable energy, and decentralized management can contribute to sustainable rural drinking water service delivery.
​​​​​​​
Fatehgarh Sahib, Punjab- Dr. Sona Thind, Deputy Commissioner
highlighted the district’s successful achievement of 100%  FHTC coverage, ensuring tap water supply to all 78,475 rural households across 429 villages, along with full coverage of schools and Anganwadi centres. Building upon this achievement, the district has shifted its focus towards maintaining service quality, with nearly 80% of rural households receiving more than 70 lpcd of water, exceeding the JJM benchmark of 55 lpcd. To address groundwater depletion and water quality concerns, the district implemented a major 12 MLD surface water project drawing water from the Rajpura Distributary. The project serves 92 villages and has significantly benefited fluoride-affected areas by providing safe drinking water to over 86,000 people through an extensive pipeline network. The district has also adopted IoT-based real-time monitoring systems and a dedicated grievance redressal mechanism to ensure continuous service delivery and prompt response to complaints. Regular DWSM meetings, community participation through Gram Panchayats and VWSCs, and structured planning have strengthened local ownership of water supply systems. A strong emphasis has been placed on water quality surveillance, with NABL-accredited laboratories conducting regular testing and women-led community monitoring through Field Testing Kits (FTKs). Through a combination of surface water infrastructure, digital monitoring, community participation, and rigorous quality testing, the district has developed a sustainable model for maintaining safe and reliable drinking water services under Jal Jeevan Mission.
North and Middle Andaman, Andaman & Nicobar Islands- Sh. Sushant Padha, Deputy Commissioner
highlighted the district's achievement of 100% FHTC coverage, covering all villages and approximately 24,400 households under Jal Jeevan Mission. A total of eight JJM schemes were completed with an expenditure of about ₹5.2 crore, ensuring universal rural water supply coverage. Given the district's unique island geography and recurring summer water scarcity, monthly DWSM meetings are being conducted to review water availability and plan long-term sustainability measures. Discussions focus on rejuvenation of existing water sources, construction of ponds, ring wells, and water treatment plants, as well as expediting Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) clearances, which often delay project implementation due to the district's extensive forest cover. To address seasonal water shortages, the district has adopted a decentralized approach by creating village-level water storage structures and enhancing local water security through convergence with MGNREGA and other development programmes. The administration is also working closely with ISRO's National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) to identify and study spring sources, assess groundwater feasibility, and improve recharge measures. The district has placed strong emphasis on water quality monitoring, with regular sample testing through WQMIS-enabled laboratories and continuous surveillance of drinking water sources. A proactive grievance redressal mechanism, supported by digital communication platforms and local stakeholder networks, helps ensure prompt resolution of complaints, including a focus on zero-leakage service delivery. Awareness campaigns on water conservation, social water audits, community training, and public outreach through print and social media are being conducted extensively to promote responsible water use and strengthen long-term source sustainability in the island district.
In his concluding remarks,
Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM
appreciated the presentations made by Districts and urged that all Mission Directors to actively participate in the upcoming Skilling and Nal Jal Mitra Programme discussions by coordinating with the State Skill Development Departments and sharing inputs before the virtual meeting scheduled on 21 September 2026. Further, he stated that States/UTs were also advised to commence geo-tagging of rural water supply sources from 2 October 2026. Further, Jal Arpan activities should be organized on 2 October 2026 across the maximum possible number of Gram Panchayats, with details of participating GPs to be shared with the Department by 20 September 2026. States/UTs were also directed to initiate post-monsoon testing of water supply sources from 2 October 2026. The meeting concluded with appreciation for the efforts of all participating States and Districts towards effective implementation of the Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.

title: Ministry of Law and Justice organises Officer-Level Awareness Workshop on Tele-Law Services at Nuh, Haryana under DISHA 2.0 Scheme

content:
The Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India, organized an Officer-Level Awareness Workshop under the Tele-Law Initiative of the DISHA 2.0 (Designing Innovative Solutions for Holistic Access to Justice) Scheme at the
Mini Secretariat, Nuh, Haryana
on
15 September 2026
. The session also emphasized the importance of leveraging digital platforms to bridge the gap between legal service providers and beneficiaries.
A live demonstration of the Tele-Law Portal and the Nyaya Setu AI-enabled chatbot was conducted to familiarize participants with the digital tools available under the scheme and to showcase how citizens can access legal information and advice through technology-driven platforms.
The Awareness workshop concluded with an interactive stakeholder discussion focusing on implementation challenges, best practices, and opportunities for expanding the reach of legal services. Participants also shared suggestions and raised queries regarding the effective delivery of Tele-Law services in their respective jurisdictions.

title: Railway Minister Inaugurates Shivlakha GCT, Dedicates Three Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals to the Nation and Lays Foundation Stone for Linch GCT
subtitle:
New GCTs to Support Faster Cargo Movement, Reduce Logistics Costs and Connect Regional Businesses with National Markets

Union Minister also Flags Off  Salt-Loaded Freight Train from Shivlakha GCT to Mithapur

Lightweight Stainless Steel Salt Containers to Make Salt Loading, Unloading and Transportation Easier
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 SEP 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Railways Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw today inaugurated, dedicated to the nation and laid the foundation stone for five Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals (GCTs) in Gujarat, strengthening the State’s freight handling capacity and improving connectivity between regional economic centres, ports and markets across the country.
Shri Vaishnaw also flagged off the  salt-loaded freight train from Shivlakha GCT to  Mithapur, marking an important step towards greater use of rail for movement of salt from Gujarat to its destination.
Among the five GCTs, the GCT at Shivlakha in Kachchh was inaugurated . The GCT at Bhimasar in Kachchh, the GCT at Devaliya in Morbi, and the GCT at Chandisar in Banaskantha were dedicated to the nation. The foundation stone was laid for the GCT at Linch in Mahesana.

#RailInfra4Gujarat
